prerequisites: Theory of Structures and Industrial Constructions
Problem-solving, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and communication skills in Industrial Engineering
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.

syllabus_topics: Block I: Theoretical Foundations of the Finite Element Method
Topic 1: Introduction to numerical methods for solving partial differential equations
Importance of numerical methods in engineering problems
Introduction to the Finite Element Method (FEM)
Topic 2: Finite Element Method for material and structure modeling
Topic 3: Isoparametric elements and numerical integration
Block II: Finite Element Simulations: practical applications
Topic 5: Introduction to commercial finite element software
Topic 7: Solving engineering problems with commercial software

assessment_methods.method: Resolution of practical cases (in computer lab sessions)
Oral presentation and defense of the project

assessment_rules: The overall pass mark is 5 out of 10. A minimum score (4 for SE1 and SE2, 5 for SE4) is required for each assessable activity to contribute to the final grade; otherwise, the grade recorded will be 4.0. 100% attendance to practical sessions (SE-2) is mandatory, with unjustified absence resulting in a 0 for the course. In the extraordinary call, students may retake or resubmit re-evaluable activities that were not passed, retaining scores for non-re-evaluable activities and already passed re-evaluable activities. If a student meets the minimum in all re-evaluable activities but still does not achieve a global score of 5, they will be re-evaluated on re-evaluable activities where they scored below 5 or, failing that, on those where they scored 5 or higher.
